top.title: Sokoto approves ₦6.12bn for nine UBEC model schools
top.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sokoto State Government has approved ₦6.12 billion for the construction of nine Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) prototype schools across the state’s three senatorial districts. The government also approved additional funds for the rehabilitation and construction of mosques and the development of Islamic educational institutions across the state. The approvals were among the major decisions reached at Wednesday’s State Executive Council meeting, presided over by Governor Ahmed Aliyu at the Government House, Sokoto. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Bashir Achida, said the nine UBEC prototype schools would be distributed equally among the three senatorial districts, with three schools allocated to each district. He said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to quality basic education, improving the learning environment and providing modern facilities for pupils, particularly in communities requiring better school infrastructure. Achida said the investment was in line with Governor Aliyu’s commitment to transforming the education sector under his administration’s Nine-Point SMART Agenda. On religious infrastructure, the council approved ₦221,548,705.25 for the rehabilitation of Achida Central Juma’at Mosque and ₦154,941,290 for the rehabilitation of Sabon Birni Central Juma’at Mosque. It also approved ₦98,242,007.50 for the construction of five daily prayer mosques in the Kwamberu area and ₦285,125,650.92 for the rehabilitation of Tureta Central Juma’at Mosque in Tureta Local Government Area. Similarly, ₦230,660,473.19 was approved for the rehabilitation of Kuppa Juma’at Mosque in the Gidan Sauro area. In the area of Islamic education, the council approved ₦166,982,489 for the construction of classrooms and sanitation facilities at Raddul Azzam Quranic School in Achida. Another ₦297,655,995.50 was approved for the construction of an Islamic school in Sabon Garin Tudun Wada area of Sokoto South Local Government Area. The commissioner further disclosed that ₦53,937,500 was approved for the provision of carpets at Gada Central Juma’at Mosque to improve facilities for congregational prayers. Achida said the approvals reflected the administration’s commitment to interventions in critical sectors, particularly basic education, religious development and community infrastructure. The projects, when completed, are expected to expand access to educational facilities, improve existing religious institutions and provide additional infrastructure for learning and worship across the state’s three senatorial districts. top.title: Edo pharmacists, consumer committee clash over drug inspections
top.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – The Edo State chapter of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has disagreed with the state Consumer Protection Committee (CPC) over the legality of the committee’s alleged entry into pharmaceutical premises to inspect and confiscate suspected expired, adulterated and counterfeit drugs. The pharmacists accused the committee of exceeding its statutory powers by conducting inspections, seizing pharmaceutical products and imposing fines on operators, insisting that the regulation of pharmacy practice is governed by federal laws. Addressing journalists in Benin City on Thursday on behalf of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN), an arm of the PSN, the state president, Pharm. Chris Oisakede, said pharmacists had established procedures for handling expired drugs in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Oisakede explained that expired medicines were not supposed to be discarded indiscriminately because of the dangers they posed to public health. “An expired drug is dangerous and poisonous, so they are usually gathered and handed over to NAFDAC, which has the protocols for destroying them,” he said. Flanked by other ACPN executives, Oisakede maintained that the CPC lacked the statutory authority to inspect, supervise or regulate pharmacy practice in the country. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Edo State CPC has no jurisdiction or authority, whether directly or indirectly, to enter, inspect, supervise or regulate the practice of pharmacy in Nigeria in any manner whatsoever. “Pharmacy practice in Nigeria, in all its aspects and ramifications, is governed by applicable federal legislation,” he said. He described community pharmacies as important healthcare facilities, noting that pharmacists counsel patients, promote the rational use of medicines, support treatment adherence, identify medicine-related problems and provide medicine safety information. The PSN consequently called on the committee to stop what it described as unauthorised pharmaceutical inspections, raids, harassment, seizures and sealing of premises, as well as the imposition of penalties where it could not establish clear statutory authority. However, reacting to the allegations, the CPC chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu, defended the committee’s enforcement activities, citing Section 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act as the legal basis for its operations. Iyamu said the provision empowered him to enter premises where there were reasonable grounds to suspect violations of the law, inspect products and examine their packaging, as well as take samples for examination. He added that the law also authorised the seizure of counterfeit, adulterated, banned or fake drugs, confiscation of unwholesome processed food products and sealing of premises connected with suspected offences. top.title: Plans to increase Windsor Park capacity to 23,750
top.description: The current capacity of Windsor Park is 18,500 [Getty Images] The planned redevelopment of Windsor Park to enable the stadium to host games at the 2035 Women's World Cup includes proposals to increase the stadium's capacity to 23,750, according to a Fifa report. A joint bid to host the tournament has been submitted by the governing bodies in England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The UK-wide bid is the only one put forward to host the tournament and is therefore set to be ratified at the Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November. Belfast's Windsor Park is the only stadium from Northern Ireland nominated as part of the bid, but in order to comply with the Fifa proposal that it could host games up until the quarter-final stage, the capacity of the venue must be increased from the current 18,500 capacity. The Fifa report said that "further redevelopment is planned, including the increase in capacity" of Windsor Park up to 23,750 by 2035. "These works are expected to enhance the stadium's suitability as a modern international venue," the report continued. "The stadium authority has committed to implementing the necessary upgrades to achieve compliance with the minimum requirements." Alongside the increase in capacity, other parts of the planned redevelopment to Windsor Park include the installation of "a hybrid‑grass system with tournament‑compliant field‑of‑play dimensions" and "an upgrade of the floodlighting system". The Irish Football Association (IFA) has been contacted for comment. The stadium was last redeveloped in 2015, when the IFA received £28.75m from the Northern Ireland Executive to bring the seating capacity up to 18,500. Plans for Northern Ireland to host matches during Euro 2028 fell through after the government said it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament. Windsor Park is one of 19 stadiums that feature in the joint bid for the 2035 World Cup, with 14 based in England, two in Scotland and two in Wales. The English based stadiums included in the bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, City Ground, Stadium of Light and Old Trafford. Easter Road and Hampden Park are the two Scottish stadiums put forward, with Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues. Brazil will host the 2027 Women's World Cup, while the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica made the sole bid for the 2031 tournament. The 2031 edition will be expanded to include 48 teams for the first time, up from 32.

top.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
top.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. top.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
top.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. top.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. top.title: Michigan State looks like a national title contender, and Jeremy Fears is the reason why
top.description: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images CHICAGO — Jeremy Fears Jr. was on a mission playing in front of his hometown crowd at the Champions Classic. Led by a brilliant effort from Fears, the National Player of the Year frontrunner, No. 5 Michigan State hit No. 2 Duke hard with the first punch and never relented during a convincing 79-73 victory on Tuesday night. While the opening matchup of college basketball’s annual November showcase looked like it might be one-sided in favor of the Blue Devils — who entered the game as nearly 7-point favorites — the Spartans opened the game on an 11-2 run, never trailed and led by double-digits for stretches of the second half. Fears put forth a strong opening salvo for an awards campaign — finishing with 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds while completely overshadowing a beleaguered Blue Devil backcourt. Perhaps most importantly, Michigan State looked like a serious national title contender with Fears receiving plenty of help from a variety of sources on both ends of the floor. The Spartans stood out in multiple ways with its impressive Champions Classic win over Duke. As Tom Izzo stood on the sidelines smiling and winking with Michigan State controlling nearly all 40 minutes, it’s clear the Spartans could be a force this season. Fears elevates his game The redemption arc was clear for Fears entering the Duke matchup at Champions Classic. Facing the Blue Devils in a non-conference game last season at the Breslin Center, Fears went a miserable 0-for-10 in a Michigan State loss — finishing with six points and 13 assists. It would have been natural for Fears to aggressively hunt his own offense early to show Duke (and the nation) how he’s evolved as a player. Instead, Fears leaned into playing his own game, finding his teammates and letting his own offense come to him later. Finishing with only three points in the first half, Fears focused on working the ball to Michigan State’s other weapons, finishing the first 20 minutes with eight assists. In the second half, Fears turned up the pressure attacking and splitting ball screens, often drawing multiple Blue Devil defenders and getting to the free-throw line on a regular basis. If Fears wasn’t feeding big men under the basket for easy dunks, finding open perimeter shooters or completely disrupting Duke’s offensive game plan, you could see the floor general facing the green-and-white sections of the United Center — repeatedly waving his arms upward to generate more noise from the Michigan State faithful. “They put me in position to be successful,” Fears said while crediting his teammates and coaching staff. “At the same time, I put the time in, I put the work in and just keep trusting whatever we’re going to do. top.title: Simon Taufel returns to lead ILT20 match officials' panel for Season 5
top.description: One of cricket's most respected match officials, Australia’s Simon Taufel, will return to lead the match officials’ panel at the ILT20 for a fifth consecutive season. The five-time ICC Umpire of the Year (2004–2008) will be the match referee for the season opener on 21 November at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, where defending champions Desert Vipers take on MI Emirates in a rematch of last season’s final. Taufel will share match referee duties through the season with Roshan Mahanama (52 Tests and 213 ODIs for Sri Lanka). New Zealand’s Chris Brown, and Martin Saggers (three Tests for England) will be the on-field umpires for the opener. Australia’s Paul Wilson will be the third umpire and New Zealand’s Wayne Knights the fourth umpire. Wilson will alternate as third umpire (TV umpire) with West Indies’ Leslie Reifer for the competition. Both have been appointed as specialist TV umpires, with the ILT20 leveraging the HE Smart Replay system to enhance the accuracy and time efficiency of third-umpire decision-making. The panel also includes ICC Elite Panel umpires Richard Illingworth (nine Tests and 25 ODIs for England) and South Africa’s Adrian Holdstock, along with Afghanistan’s Ahmad Pakteen. Aasif Iqbal, Akbar Ali Khan and Shiju Mannil represent the UAE. To help develop officiating in the region, and as part of their wider partnership, the ILT20 will invite two umpires each from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia to shadow the panel during the league stage. They will attend matches to gain first-hand exposure to officiating at a higher level. The programme will be supported by former ICC Umpires Coach Dennis Burns. Ahead of the season, Taufel said: “It’s a privilege to return for a fifth season of the ILT20. We’re strengthened this year by ICC Elite Panel umpires Richard Illingworth and Adrian Holdstock, alongside Roshan Mahanama, talented umpires from across the world, and an ever-improving group of UAE officials. Our focus remains to keep the spotlight on the players and the quality of cricket through officiating excellence.” On the programme for Kuwaiti and Saudi umpires, Taufel added: “Bringing umpires from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia into our environment is a really exciting step for officiating in the region. Working alongside an international panel and learning from someone like Dennis Burns will give them exposure they can take back home and build on.” The updated Season 5 Playing Conditions also take effect from the opening match. The biggest on-field change is a new “batter zone” for judging wides on both sides, and umpires have been told to apply it strictly to stop negative bowling. The 60-second stop clock between overs now applies to the batting side as well. After two warnings in an innings, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. ILT20 Season 5 will feature some of the game’s biggest stars, including Moeen Ali, Usman Tariq and Finn Allen (Abu Dhabi Knight Riders), Babar Azam, Shimron Hetmyer and Naseem Shah (Desert Vipers)

nigeria.title: Sokoto approves ₦6.12bn for nine UBEC model schools
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sokoto State Government has approved ₦6.12 billion for the construction of nine Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) prototype schools across the state’s three senatorial districts. The government also approved additional funds for the rehabilitation and construction of mosques and the development of Islamic educational institutions across the state. The approvals were among the major decisions reached at Wednesday’s State Executive Council meeting, presided over by Governor Ahmed Aliyu at the Government House, Sokoto. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Bashir Achida, said the nine UBEC prototype schools would be distributed equally among the three senatorial districts, with three schools allocated to each district. He said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to quality basic education, improving the learning environment and providing modern facilities for pupils, particularly in communities requiring better school infrastructure. Achida said the investment was in line with Governor Aliyu’s commitment to transforming the education sector under his administration’s Nine-Point SMART Agenda. On religious infrastructure, the council approved ₦221,548,705.25 for the rehabilitation of Achida Central Juma’at Mosque and ₦154,941,290 for the rehabilitation of Sabon Birni Central Juma’at Mosque. It also approved ₦98,242,007.50 for the construction of five daily prayer mosques in the Kwamberu area and ₦285,125,650.92 for the rehabilitation of Tureta Central Juma’at Mosque in Tureta Local Government Area. Similarly, ₦230,660,473.19 was approved for the rehabilitation of Kuppa Juma’at Mosque in the Gidan Sauro area. In the area of Islamic education, the council approved ₦166,982,489 for the construction of classrooms and sanitation facilities at Raddul Azzam Quranic School in Achida. Another ₦297,655,995.50 was approved for the construction of an Islamic school in Sabon Garin Tudun Wada area of Sokoto South Local Government Area. The commissioner further disclosed that ₦53,937,500 was approved for the provision of carpets at Gada Central Juma’at Mosque to improve facilities for congregational prayers. Achida said the approvals reflected the administration’s commitment to interventions in critical sectors, particularly basic education, religious development and community infrastructure. The projects, when completed, are expected to expand access to educational facilities, improve existing religious institutions and provide additional infrastructure for learning and worship across the state’s three senatorial districts. nigeria.title: Edo pharmacists, consumer committee clash over drug inspections
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – The Edo State chapter of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has disagreed with the state Consumer Protection Committee (CPC) over the legality of the committee’s alleged entry into pharmaceutical premises to inspect and confiscate suspected expired, adulterated and counterfeit drugs. The pharmacists accused the committee of exceeding its statutory powers by conducting inspections, seizing pharmaceutical products and imposing fines on operators, insisting that the regulation of pharmacy practice is governed by federal laws. Addressing journalists in Benin City on Thursday on behalf of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN), an arm of the PSN, the state president, Pharm. Chris Oisakede, said pharmacists had established procedures for handling expired drugs in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Oisakede explained that expired medicines were not supposed to be discarded indiscriminately because of the dangers they posed to public health. “An expired drug is dangerous and poisonous, so they are usually gathered and handed over to NAFDAC, which has the protocols for destroying them,” he said. Flanked by other ACPN executives, Oisakede maintained that the CPC lacked the statutory authority to inspect, supervise or regulate pharmacy practice in the country. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Edo State CPC has no jurisdiction or authority, whether directly or indirectly, to enter, inspect, supervise or regulate the practice of pharmacy in Nigeria in any manner whatsoever. “Pharmacy practice in Nigeria, in all its aspects and ramifications, is governed by applicable federal legislation,” he said. He described community pharmacies as important healthcare facilities, noting that pharmacists counsel patients, promote the rational use of medicines, support treatment adherence, identify medicine-related problems and provide medicine safety information. The PSN consequently called on the committee to stop what it described as unauthorised pharmaceutical inspections, raids, harassment, seizures and sealing of premises, as well as the imposition of penalties where it could not establish clear statutory authority. However, reacting to the allegations, the CPC chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu, defended the committee’s enforcement activities, citing Section 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act as the legal basis for its operations. Iyamu said the provision empowered him to enter premises where there were reasonable grounds to suspect violations of the law, inspect products and examine their packaging, as well as take samples for examination. He added that the law also authorised the seizure of counterfeit, adulterated, banned or fake drugs, confiscation of unwholesome processed food products and sealing of premises connected with suspected offences. nigeria.title: One dead, four wounded in Washington shooting
nigeria.description: One person was killed and four others wounded after a gunman opened fire in an upscale neighbourhood of Washington, DC, on Thursday before barricading himself inside his apartment and taking his own life, police said. The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, triggered a massive security response, with dozens of police vehicles deployed to the scene and helicopters hovering overhead. Washington’s interim police chief, Jeffery Carroll, told reporters that the gunman shot and killed one person at a fitness centre attached to his apartment building before wounding four others. He said the suspect subsequently barricaded himself inside his apartment and fired at least twice at police officers through the apartment door before shooting himself. The suspect, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, was pronounced dead at the scene. Carroll said preliminary information suggested that the gunman had been involved in “some sort of a conflict” with the homeowners association of the apartment building in the Logan Circle neighbourhood. One of the four injured victims was in critical condition, while the injuries sustained by the others did not appear to be life-threatening, the police chief said. Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser condemned the incident as a “senseless act of gun violence” and disclosed that the White House had been briefed on the shooting. The incident occurred during the busy morning rush hour, causing major traffic disruptions as police cordoned off streets around the area. Police evacuated some residents from nearby buildings, while others were instructed to remain indoors. The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying he was exercising on a treadmill when the shooting began. Michael Carney said he heard a “pop” before noticing a person lying on the gym floor with a gunshot wound to the head. “Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff,” Carney told the newspaper. Logan Circle is one of Washington’s most expensive neighbourhoods, known for its upscale restaurants and nightlife venues. The area is also located a short distance from several foreign embassies. nigeria.title: Budget Minister challenges LGs to justify monthly allocations
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Folarin Kehinde ABUJA – The Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, has challenged local governments to justify their monthly Federation Account allocations by turning them into tangible development rather than merely sharing the money. Bagudu said councils must identify economic opportunities in their communities, attract investments and create wealth instead of depending solely on statutory allocations. He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the 9th annual national conference of the Association of Local Government Vice Chairmen of Nigeria (ALGOVC), themed, “Strengthening Local Government Control for Effective National Security and Economic Growth”. Bagudu said the Federal Government was adopting a bottom-up approach through the Renewed Hope Ward Development Plan to identify local resources, investment opportunities and development needs. “Local government is not just an administrative centre that should disburse money coming from the Federation Account. That is a big error that we have been making in the past. “It is a centre that should draw attention to the blessings and the prosperity and the opportunities and potentials that are in that local government, and appropriately support that local government,” he said. He urged councillors to identify the economic potential of their wards, adding that systematic mapping would provide data for attracting investors and developing practical economic plans. Bagudu identified agriculture, fisheries and livestock as sectors capable of transforming local economies but constrained by poor farming methods, inadequate inputs and outdated practices. Citing an estimated 42 million Nigerian households engaged in agriculture, he said improved productivity could raise household incomes and stimulate economic growth. He urged vice-chairmen to identify challenges in their councils and present evidence-based demands to the Federal Government and development partners. Earlier, ALGOVC National Chairperson, Amb. Uju Okolo, called for unity, accountability and inclusive leadership, pledging to promote justice, restore confidence and ensure no member was left behind. The conference also took a political turn when the association’s Board of Trustees Chairman, Hon. Lawrence Onuchukwu, moved a motion endorsing President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027. Seconded by Okolo, the motion was adopted through a voice vote. The association also pledged support for the ruling party at the federal and state levels and appealed to Tinubu to reappoint Bagudu as minister if re-elected. nigeria.title: 2027: INEC to simulate presidential election in nationwide mock vote
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) plans to conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28 to test preparations for the 2027 general elections, Chairman Joash Amupitan has said. Amupitan announced the plan at a conference at Chatham House in London on Thursday, held to discuss “Democratic trajectory beyond the ballot” ahead of the elections. He said the exercise would simulate the forthcoming presidential election and test the commission’s readiness to transmit results. “On the 28th of this month, we are planning a mock accreditation and voting across all the states in Nigeria, so that we simulate a presidential election and just be sure that we have gotten it right and that there will be transmission of result,” Amupitan said. He also said the commission had reviewed lessons from previous elections and taken steps to address identified problems, citing recent off-cycle elections, including those in Anambra and Osun, as examples of improvements in the electoral process. “Nigerians must trust me because I’ve done off-cycle elections, and you agreed the last election in Osun State, there was improvement, and I said every election is a lesson. 2023 election was a great lesson for Nigeria. The one we had in Anambra was another. So we’ve learned certain things, and as a commission, we sat down to address some of those issues, and we have taken steps one after the other,” he said. Amupitan said INEC was working to improve logistics so voting and result declaration could be completed promptly as he pointed to the Anambra election, where results were declared the day after voting. “We are trying to improve on logistics to ensure that everything is done within the day, and then result. Look at the way we did an Anambra election. By the following day, we declared the result,” he said. He also cited recent off-cycle elections in the Federal Capital Territory and Osun, where he said results were declared the following day and voters observed the functioning of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the transmission of results. “In FCT, the same thing. In Osun, that used to be a serious problem, that the whole world thought that the whole country will collapse with Osun election the following day, the result was declared, and everybody saw the functioning of B-VAS and the transmission of results,” Amupitan added. He said the mock exercise and other measures were intended to prevent a repeat of past problems, adding that transparency and the ability to audit the process were essential. “So those are things and steps that we have taken to ensure that we don’t go back to the mistake of the past. nigeria.title: US withdraws from FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The United States has withdrawn its men’s Under-17 team from the FIFA World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns after a State Department advisory warned Americans to reconsider travel because of the risk of armed conflict. In a letter to players seen by Reuters, US Soccer said it had cancelled the team’s pre-tournament camp and participation “in light of current circumstances”. The federation cited the State Department’s Level 3 travel advisory for Qatar, updated last month, as well as related directives for embassy staff and their families. The advisory referred to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian airports and critical infrastructure, and warned that hostilities could escalate. US Soccer said it would notify players’ clubs and asked players not to comment publicly until FIFA announced the withdrawal. The 48-team tournament is scheduled to run from November 19 to December 13. The United States had been due to open against Montenegro on November 21, before facing Chile and Algeria in Group J. FIFA told Reuters it had been informed of the decision and would follow the tournament regulations. The governing body said its security assessments remained unchanged and that no new developments had affected the security situation around the tournament. FIFA added that it remained in contact with relevant authorities and looked forward to the tournament, noting that Qatar had hosted several international events in recent months. The United States reached the round of 32 at last year’s edition, also held in Qatar. The country is set to host the tournament annually through 2029. nigeria.title: 2027: INEC begins deploying non-sensitive materials
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has begun deploying non-sensitive materials to the zones as it prepares for the 2027 general election. Acting Chairman of the commission, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at a benchmarking meeting with a delegation of Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission IEBC. “Right now, all non-sensitive materials are almost ready. In fact, today as we speak here, the non-sensitive materials have been lifted to some zones now,” Gumus said. She said the commission had completed nine of its scheduled activities and was preparing for the next phase. “We are preparing for the election next year and we have activities lined up. So far, we have been able to complete nine activities and we are still preparing for the next level of activities,” she said. Gumus said the commission’s leadership had just concluded a tour of the country’s six zones to assess their level of preparedness. “The purpose was to go round the zones to see how prepared we are, assess what the zones have put in place, their challenges and what to do. We concluded last week and we can see from our tour that we are really going towards the election proper,” she said. On Permanent Voter Cards PVCs, the acting chairman said production had been completed and distribution to the states was well advanced. “As of today, we can say that PVCs have been produced and the first, second batches, most of the states have received them. Their PVC collection is ongoing. All those who are supposed to be the voters are supposed to receive their PVCs, and if they don’t have them, it is also another challenge,” Gumus said. She added that capacity building was under way for staff at the headquarters and in the states, and that the procurement and deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS devices were also ongoing. On diaspora voting, Gumus said the commission could not proceed for now because the law did not provide for it. “Here, because we go by the law, in our electoral law, it is not included there, so we cannot go on for the diaspora voting for now until we amend the electoral law,” she said. The acting chairman said the commission had arranged for its directors to hold an interactive session with the Kenyan team and present papers on the work of their departments. Leading the delegation, the Kenyan High Commissioner to Nigeria, Isaac Parashina, said the IEBC team was in Nigeria to benchmark ahead of Kenya’s general election in August 2027. He said the team was studying how Nigeria handled its diaspora population and special voting groups, as Kenya sought to widen voting rights for citizens living abroad. “Currently we have about 12 of them who voted in the last general election, but there is intention to expand to around, I think, 26,” Parashina said, referring to the countries where Kenyans abroad vote. nigeria.title: Insecurity: Atiku tackles Tinubu as 638 are killed, 64,000 flee Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu of failing in his fundamental duty to protect Nigerians, following reports that 638 people were killed in insecurity-related incidents in October, while nearly 64,000 others fled violence in northern Nigeria to neighbouring Niger. The figures highlight the scale of the security crisis confronting the country, with Atiku demanding urgent action from the Federal Government to halt the killings, protect vulnerable communities and account for its efforts to restore public safety. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the figures as a devastating indictment of the country’s security situation. “Behind every number is a Nigerian whose life has been lost, a family in mourning or a community forced to abandon its home. Nigerians should not have to flee across our borders to find safety,” he said. The Centre for Democracy and Development’s October tracker recorded 638 deaths in broader insecurity incidents during the month, with the North-East accounting for 409. Across all security incidents, the figure stood at 640, up from 396 in September. The United Nations also reported that nearly 64,000 people had fled violence in northern Nigeria to Niger since the beginning of 2026, while several hundred others crossed into Benin. Calling for stronger security operations and support for displaced families, Atiku urged the Federal Government to work with neighbouring countries and humanitarian agencies to assist those forced to flee. “The Tinubu administration must make the protection of lives and communities its first responsibility. It must strengthen security in affected areas, support displaced families and work with neighbouring countries and humanitarian agencies to assist those who have fled. Nigerians also deserve a clear account of what is being done to stop the killings and restore safety,” he said. He challenged Tinubu to take responsibility for the worsening security situation rather than offer further explanations. “A government that cannot protect its people has failed in its most basic duty. President Tinubu must stop offering excuses and take responsibility for this worsening crisis. Nigerians need safety now, not another promise,” Atiku said. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. sports.title: Plans to increase Windsor Park capacity to 23,750
sports.description: The current capacity of Windsor Park is 18,500 [Getty Images] The planned redevelopment of Windsor Park to enable the stadium to host games at the 2035 Women's World Cup includes proposals to increase the stadium's capacity to 23,750, according to a Fifa report. A joint bid to host the tournament has been submitted by the governing bodies in England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The UK-wide bid is the only one put forward to host the tournament and is therefore set to be ratified at the Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November. Belfast's Windsor Park is the only stadium from Northern Ireland nominated as part of the bid, but in order to comply with the Fifa proposal that it could host games up until the quarter-final stage, the capacity of the venue must be increased from the current 18,500 capacity. The Fifa report said that "further redevelopment is planned, including the increase in capacity" of Windsor Park up to 23,750 by 2035. "These works are expected to enhance the stadium's suitability as a modern international venue," the report continued. "The stadium authority has committed to implementing the necessary upgrades to achieve compliance with the minimum requirements." Alongside the increase in capacity, other parts of the planned redevelopment to Windsor Park include the installation of "a hybrid‑grass system with tournament‑compliant field‑of‑play dimensions" and "an upgrade of the floodlighting system". The Irish Football Association (IFA) has been contacted for comment. The stadium was last redeveloped in 2015, when the IFA received £28.75m from the Northern Ireland Executive to bring the seating capacity up to 18,500. Plans for Northern Ireland to host matches during Euro 2028 fell through after the government said it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament. Windsor Park is one of 19 stadiums that feature in the joint bid for the 2035 World Cup, with 14 based in England, two in Scotland and two in Wales. The English based stadiums included in the bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, City Ground, Stadium of Light and Old Trafford. Easter Road and Hampden Park are the two Scottish stadiums put forward, with Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues. Brazil will host the 2027 Women's World Cup, while the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica made the sole bid for the 2031 tournament. The 2031 edition will be expanded to include 48 teams for the first time, up from 32.

sports.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. sports.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. sports.title: Simon Taufel returns to lead ILT20 match officials' panel for Season 5
sports.description: One of cricket's most respected match officials, Australia’s Simon Taufel, will return to lead the match officials’ panel at the ILT20 for a fifth consecutive season. The five-time ICC Umpire of the Year (2004–2008) will be the match referee for the season opener on 21 November at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, where defending champions Desert Vipers take on MI Emirates in a rematch of last season’s final. Taufel will share match referee duties through the season with Roshan Mahanama (52 Tests and 213 ODIs for Sri Lanka). New Zealand’s Chris Brown, and Martin Saggers (three Tests for England) will be the on-field umpires for the opener. Australia’s Paul Wilson will be the third umpire and New Zealand’s Wayne Knights the fourth umpire. Wilson will alternate as third umpire (TV umpire) with West Indies’ Leslie Reifer for the competition. Both have been appointed as specialist TV umpires, with the ILT20 leveraging the HE Smart Replay system to enhance the accuracy and time efficiency of third-umpire decision-making. The panel also includes ICC Elite Panel umpires Richard Illingworth (nine Tests and 25 ODIs for England) and South Africa’s Adrian Holdstock, along with Afghanistan’s Ahmad Pakteen. Aasif Iqbal, Akbar Ali Khan and Shiju Mannil represent the UAE. To help develop officiating in the region, and as part of their wider partnership, the ILT20 will invite two umpires each from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia to shadow the panel during the league stage. They will attend matches to gain first-hand exposure to officiating at a higher level. The programme will be supported by former ICC Umpires Coach Dennis Burns. Ahead of the season, Taufel said: “It’s a privilege to return for a fifth season of the ILT20. We’re strengthened this year by ICC Elite Panel umpires Richard Illingworth and Adrian Holdstock, alongside Roshan Mahanama, talented umpires from across the world, and an ever-improving group of UAE officials. Our focus remains to keep the spotlight on the players and the quality of cricket through officiating excellence.” On the programme for Kuwaiti and Saudi umpires, Taufel added: “Bringing umpires from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia into our environment is a really exciting step for officiating in the region. Working alongside an international panel and learning from someone like Dennis Burns will give them exposure they can take back home and build on.” The updated Season 5 Playing Conditions also take effect from the opening match. The biggest on-field change is a new “batter zone” for judging wides on both sides, and umpires have been told to apply it strictly to stop negative bowling. The 60-second stop clock between overs now applies to the batting side as well. After two warnings in an innings, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. ILT20 Season 5 will feature some of the game’s biggest stars, including Moeen Ali, Usman Tariq and Finn Allen (Abu Dhabi Knight Riders), Babar Azam, Shimron Hetmyer and Naseem Shah (Desert Vipers)

sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the large majority of New York Yankees fans welcome the idea of moving on from infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr., a new rumor may suggest that letting him walk in MLB free agency is a mistake. There is no doubt that Chisholm Jr. has talent. He is a two-time All-Star who has a legit power bat and the rare skill set to be a 30-30 (home runs and stolen bases) player when he is hitting on all cylinders. Furthermore, he is a versatile fielder who can play multiple positions on the infield and outfield and is still in his 20s. There is also no doubt that he can be a locker room problem. The Yankees knew that when they traded for him two years ago. But it was worth the risk because of his talent. However, his immaturity, lack of focus on defense, and a down season in 2026 have soured opinions about him among New York fans. Yet, despite the obvious red flags in his character and baseball skills, it seems that Chisholm Jr. has fast become one of the most sought-after players in free agency. According to MLB Network’s Jon Morosi, eleven teams are in discussions with Chisholm Jr.’s representatives , and “multiple in-person meetings are being scheduled next week.” If nearly a dozen teams are interested in the 28-year-old, are the Yankees making the wrong move by letting him walk? Are the New York Yankees making a mistake by letting Jazz Chisholm walk? Garcia Jr. is absolutely a better hitter, but there is a reason the Washington Nationals moved him from second to first base. A case could certainly be made that, with a different manager or stronger leadership in the clubhouse, the negative parts of Chisholm Jr.’s personality could be held in check, so his positive energy and passion could be a huge plus for the team. Yet, neither is coming in 2027. That is why the Yankees are not making a mistake by letting the infielder take his talents elsewhere. technology.title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
technology.description: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. technology.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
technology.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationship with another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. A two-week downfall News of the scandal first broke barely a couple of weeks ago, on October 29, when claims surfaced that Huang had been the target of an espionage plot involving a Chinese businesswoman working for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed which was a customer of Nvidia. According to the New York Times , US intelligence had reason to believe the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to gather information about Nvidia and its operations for the Beijing government. Megaspeed also faces claims it was illicitly shipping Nvidia products to China, in violation of US export controls. Any relationship between Huang and a Chinese operative would be enormously concerning, as the US has been trying to keep advanced technology for AI out of the hands of the country, allegedly for security reasons, fearing it might be used for military purposes. For its part, Beijing rejects the spying allegations, saying they are part of a smear campaign against China. Shortly after Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating Huang, he sent an email to Nvidia staff apologizing and confessing to having an affair, though he did not explicitly name Alice Huang in his public apology. It seemed like the leather-jacketed leader might just hang on, since it was difficult to imagine anyone other than him leading the company after all this time. But Nvidia’s shares fell 4.3 percent on November 9 and a further 5.5 percent the following day, wiping around $430 billion off its market value, amid all the speculation. Then the claim emerged regarding a second affair, with an employee at Nvidia who reported to him, and many commentators took it as a sign the game was up. Huang resigned the same day the news broke. Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens. "In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis. "To secure a stable future for her brother, she assumes one final identity and is forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who’s confronting the end of her life. The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn." This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight! "You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop. Will "Blade Runner 2099" usher in a new era for the sci-fi franchise? (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099 " sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Delivered by creator and showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls"), and executive produced by Silka Louisa and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" lands on Prime Video beginning Nov. 25, 2026 .

science.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
science.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. science.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
science.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

science.title: Vast data dump from Euclid space telescope reveals stunning galaxies
science.description: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The European Space Agency has just released a vast batch of observations of the sky captured by the Euclid space telescope. Launched in 2023, the telescope is currently on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to build the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos ever created . The latest observations – catchily titled DR1-Foundation – cover an area of the sky as big as 9500 full moons. The collection includes 900 million galaxies. The mosaic of 740 images at the top of the article, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, covers 367 square degrees of the northern sky. At full resolution, this snapshot runs to 500 gigapixels. Advertisement The bright oval in the lower left portion of the patchwork image is the spiral galaxy Messier 81, which is some 12 million light years from Earth. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Messier 81 in greater detail, along with part of the M81 group of galaxies that also bears its name – an honour bestowed on it as the largest galaxy of the bunch. To the lower left is the smaller galaxy NGC 3077, and the patches of wispy blue cloud throughout the images are galactic cirrus, which are actually in the foreground and part of our own home galaxy. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO Here, Messier 81 is shown in even greater detail, in an image taken at the full resolution available to Euclid. The haze dominating the right side of the frame is the disc of Messier 81, inside which individual stars are visible. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO This hazy galaxy is NGC 1291, around 33 million light years away. The image was made from two taken by Euclid and then cropped. In the background, even more distant galaxies are visible – the furthest away of which show up in red. Stars are still actively forming within NGC 1291, and can be seen as small blue-hued dots. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies lying around 800 million light years away. The cluster is home to a diverse array of galaxies, including whirling spirals and fuzzy ellipticals. In the centre of the image is a strong gravitational lens, where the light travelling to us from a more distant galaxy has been warped by a massive object in the foreground.

science.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
science.description: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Here are some of the best places to watch the moon's shadow cross what was once the Roman Empire. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Baelo Claudia, Spain Baelo Claudia's Roman ruins overlook Bolonia beach and the Strait of Gibraltar. (Image credit: Andrea Pucci via Getty Images) Location: near Tarifa, Andalucía, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:44 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 31 seconds Historical cloud cover: 12% Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east Roman ruins, an Atlantic beach and the mountains of Africa could all share the frame with the eclipsed sun at Baelo Claudia. Founded in the second century B.C., this remarkably well-preserved Roman city near Bolonia beach includes a forum, basilica, theater, temples, baths and a decumanus maximus (east-west street), all set against forested hills and a vast coastal sand dune. For photographers, the possibilities are exceptional — columns and temples may provide an ancient foreground, while wider compositions could incorporate the beach and dunes. On particularly clear days, Morocco is visible across the Strait of Gibraltar — potentially putting Roman ruins, two continents and a total solar eclipse into one extraordinary scene. 2. Málaga Roman Theatre, Spain The Roman Theatre at the foot of the Málaga Alcazaba dates back to the 1st century BC. (Image credit: Manfred Gottschalk via Getty Images) Location: Málaga, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 1 minute, 57 seconds Historical cloud cover: 9% Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east Few eclipse locations can offer two civilizations in the same photograph. Málaga's Roman Theatre was built in the first century B.C., when the city was part of the Roman province of Hispania, and today sits directly beneath the Alcazaba, the imposing Muslim-era palace-fortress that dominates the hillside above.
